questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 32 + 24 × 4 ÷ 16 – 64 = 90
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

32 + 24 × 4 ÷ 16 – 64 = 90
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

Option 1) : + and × 

Given equation : 32 + 24 × 4 ÷ 16 – 64 = 90

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 32 × 24 + 4 ÷ 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 32 × 24 + 4 ÷ 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 32 × 24 + 0.25 - 64 = 90

⇒ 768 + 0.25 - 64 = 90

⇒ 768.25 - 64 = 90

⇒ 704.25 ≠ 90

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : ÷ and +

Given equation : 32 + 24 × 4 ÷ 16 – 64 = 90

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 32 ÷ 24 × 4 + 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 32 ÷ 24 × 4 + 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 1.333 × 4 + 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 5.333 + 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 21.333 - 64 = 90

⇒ - 42.666 ≠ 90

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : ÷ and ×

Given equation : 32 + 24 × 4 ÷ 16 – 64 = 90

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 32 + 24 ÷ 4 × 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 32 + 24 ÷ 4 × 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 32 + 6 × 16 - 64 = 90

⇒ 32 + 96 - 64 = 90

⇒ 128 - 64 = 90

⇒ 64 ≠ 90

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : + and –

Given equation : 32 + 24 × 4 ÷ 16 – 64 = 90

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation is as follows : 32 - 24 × 4 ÷ 16 + 64 = 90

⇒ 32 - 24 × 4 ÷ 16 + 64 = 90

⇒ 32 - 24 × 0.25 + 64 = 90

⇒ 32 - 6 + 64 = 90

⇒ 96 - 6 = 90

⇒ 90 = 90

LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "+ and –".

Given expression is : 8 B (4 A 5) C (99 A 27) D 14 A 5 B (112 D 16)

= 8 × (4 + 5) - (99 + 27) ÷ 14 + 5 × (112 ÷ 16)

= 8 × 9 - 126 ÷ 14 + 5 × 7

= 8 × 9 - 9 + 5 × 7

= 72 - 9 + 35

= 107 - 9

= 98

Hence, the correct answer is "98".

questions.question: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two numbers of the following number-pair. 14 : 450
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two numbers of the following number-pair.

14 : 450
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:-

(First number + 1)2 × 2 = Second Number

  • 14 : 450 

= (14 + 1)2 × 2 = 450

= (15)2 × 2 = 450

= 225 × 2 = 450

= 450 = 450

Similarly,

  • 18 : 722

= (18 + 1)2 × 2 = 722

= (19)2 × 2 = 722

= 361 × 2 = 722

= 722 = 722

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Alternate Method

First number × ((First number + 2) × 2) + 2 = Second number.

By using BODMAS RULE :

  • 14 : 450 

= 14 × ((14 + 2) × 2) + 2

= 14 × (16 × 2) + 2

= 14 × 32 + 2

= 448 + 2

= 450

Similarly,

  • 18 : 722

= 18 × ((18 + 2) × 2) + 2

= 18 × (20 × 2) + 2

= 18 × 40 + 2

= 720 + 2

= 722

Hence, the correct answer is "18 : 722".

questions.question: The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in a given year or period is defined as ______.
questions.questionHtml: The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in a given year or period is defined as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is neonatal mortality rate.

Key Points

  • The number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in a given year or period is defined as the neonatal mortality rate.
  • There are some concerns about the quality of neonatal mortality reporting both internationally and within states, particularly in terms of defining a live birth and/or reporting both birth and death certificates for newborns with very low birth weights.
  • When neonatal death certificates are matched to corresponding birth certificates, much more additional and valuable data (birth weight, mother's smoking status, when prenatal care began, etc.) is obtained for neonatal mortality risk analysis.

Important Points

  • The number of newborn deaths per 1,000 live births is known as the infant mortality rate.
  • The infant mortality rate is an essential indicator of a society's general health, in addition to providing crucial information regarding maternal and baby health.
  • The crude mortality rate is derived by dividing the number of fatalities in a particular time by the number of people who were at risk of dying during that period.
  • A death rate that is limited to a certain age group is known as an age-specific mortality rate.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the mountains? I- Mountains may be arranged in a line known as range. Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the mountains?

I- Mountains may be arranged in a line known as range.

II- The Aravali range in India is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world.

III- Mt. Kilimanjaro in South America is an example of a Volcanic Mountain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only I and II.

Key Points

  • Mountains are sometimes organised in a line called a range. Many mountain ranges are made up of a series of parallel ranges that stretch for hundreds of kilometres sometimes such a line known as a mountain range. Hence statement 1 is correct.
  • The Himalayas, Alps, and the Andes are Asian, European, and South American mountain ranges, respectively.
  • The Aravallis in Northwestern India are one of the world's oldest fold mountains, forming remnant mountains with elevations ranging from 300 to 900 metres. Hence statement 2 is correct.
  • They reach 800 kilometres from Gujarat's Himmatnagar to Delhi's 692 kilometres, encompassing Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Delhi. 
  • At 5,895 metres, Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa's tallest mountain (19,340 feet).
  • It is the world's tallest free-standing mountain rise, meaning it exists independently of any mountain range.
  • Kilimanjaro, also known as a stratovolcano (a big volcano comprised of ash, lava, and rock), is made up of three cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira.
  •  Mt. Kilimanjaro is a volcanic mountain but it lies in Africa, not in South America.. Hence statement 3 is incorrect.
  • The mountain's top and the tallest of the three volcanic structures is Kibo.

questions.question: The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the ______ Constitution.
questions.questionHtml: The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the ______ Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is British.

Key Points

  • The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the British Constitution. 
  • The Government of India Act of 1919, commonly known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, took effect in 1921.
  • It was the first time in the country that bicameralism and direct elections were implemented.
  • The Indian Legislative Council was therefore replaced with a bicameral legislature with an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).
  • Direct election was used to elect the majority of members of both Houses.

Important Points

  • Republic
  • Ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble
Canada
  • Federation with a strong Centre
  • Vesting of residuary powers in the Centre
  • Appointment of state governors by the Centre
  • Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court

questions.question: Poor sanitation conditions may NOT be the likely reason behind which of the following diseases/conditions?
questions.questionHtml: Poor sanitation conditions may NOT be the likely reason behind which of the following diseases/conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arthritis.

Key Points

  • Poor sanitation conditions may NOT be the likely reason behind Arthritis.
  • Arthritis is a condition in which one or more joints enlarge and become tender. Joint pain and stiffness are the most common symptoms of arthritis, which normally worsen with age.
  • Osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis are the two most frequent kinds of arthritis. Cartilage — the firm, slippery tissue that covers the ends of bones where they form a joint — breaks down as a result of osteoarthritis.
  • Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune illness in which the immune system destroys the joints, starting with the lining.
  • Diarrhoeal disorders including cholera and dysentery, as well as typhoid, intestinal worm infections, and polio, are all connected to poor sanitation. Stunting is exacerbated by poor nutrition, which also leads to the spread of antibiotic resistance.
  • Children are in danger of childhood infections and malnutrition as a result of poor sanitation, which can have a negative influence on their general development, learning, and, later in life, economic opportunities.

Additional Information

  • The poliovirus causes polio, a debilitating and potentially fatal disease. The virus can infect a person's spinal cord, causing paralysis (the inability to move parts of the body).
  • Typhoid fever is a bacterial infection that can infect multiple organs and spread throughout the body.
  • Cholera is a bacterial infection that is spread by drinking contaminated water.

questions.question: ______ refers to a sanitation system in which toilets collect human excreta in sealable, removable cartridges that are transported to treatment facilities.
questions.questionHtml: ______ refers to a sanitation system in which toilets collect human excreta in sealable, removable cartridges that are transported to treatment facilities.
questions.solution:
• Container-based sanitation (CBS) is a sanitation method in which toilets collect human waste and transport it to treatment facilities in sealable, removable containers (also known as cartridges).
  • This method of sanitation entails the use of a commercial service that offers specific types of portable toilets and distributes empty containers when full ones are picked up. The service carries excreta and carefully disposes of or reuses it.
  • The users are normally responsible for the cost of excreta collection. CBS can be utilised to offer low-income urban areas safe collection, transportation, and treatment of faeces at a lesser cost than establishing and maintaining sewers with the right development, support, and collaborations.
  • Sanitation systems based on containers are a low-cost option. They can be employed in quickly increasing cities, refugee camps, and disaster relief circumstances.
  • They are in line with Sustainable Development Goal 6 of the United Nations, which is to "provide sanitation for all by 2030."

questions.question: Why is water fluoridation, which is the controlled adjustment of fluoride to public water supply, done?
questions.questionHtml: Why is water fluoridation, which is the controlled adjustment of fluoride to public water supply, done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is To prevent tooth decay.

Key Points

  • Water fluoridation is the addition of fluoride to a public water supply with the express purpose of preventing tooth decay.
  • Fluoridated water contains a sufficient amount of fluoride to prevent cavities; this can occur naturally or through the addition of fluoride.
  • Fluoridated water works on dental surfaces by producing low levels of fluoride in saliva, which slows the demineralization of tooth enamel and speeds up the remineralization of tooth enamel in the early stages of cavities.
  • In most industrialised countries, tooth decay is still a serious public health concern, impacting 60–90 percent of kids and the vast majority of adults.
  • Fluoridation of drinking water decreases cavities in children, but its effectiveness in adults is unclear.​

Additional Information

  • Damage to a tooth's surface, or enamel, is known as tooth decay.
  • It occurs when oral bacteria produce acids that destroy the enamel.
  • Cavities (dental caries) are holes in your teeth caused by tooth decay.
  • If left untreated, dental decay can lead to discomfort, infection, and even tooth loss.

questions.question: The efforts of Siddhendra Yogi have brought glory to the dance form called ______.
questions.questionHtml: The efforts of Siddhendra Yogi have brought glory to the dance form called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

Key Points

  • Kuchipudi is one of India's eight primary classical dance forms. It comes from Kuchipudi, a village in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
  • It is a dance-drama genre that originated in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit scripture Natya Shastra.
  • Like all of India's great classical dances, it began as a religious art form tied to itinerant bards, temples, and spiritual beliefs.
  • Copper inscriptions from the 10th century and books like the Machupalli Kaifat from the 15th century show that Kuchipudi existed in an earlier iteration.
  • According to Kuchipudi legend, in the 17th century, Tirtha Narayana Yati, an Advaita Vedanta Sanyasin, and his disciple, an orphan named Siddhendra Yogi, developed and systematised the present style of Kuchipudi.

Important Points

  • Mohiniyattam is an Indian traditional dance genre that originated in Kerala and has remained popular ever since. Mohiniyattam dance takes its name from Mohini, a historical enchantress avatar of the Hindu God Vishnu who uses her feminine skills to assist good triumph over evil.
  • Kathakali is a popular genre of Indian classical dance. It's a "story play" kind of art, but it's differentiated by the traditionally male actor-dancer's lavishly colourful make-up, costumes, and face masks.
  • Bharatanatyam is a significant Hindu form of Indian classical dance. The initial origins of Bharatanatyam are regarded to be Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and Nandikeshvara's Abhinaya Darpana.

questions.question: What is the greatest number by which when 156, 181 and 331 are divided, the remainder is 6 in each case?
questions.questionHtml: What is the greatest number by which when 156, 181 and 331 are divided, the remainder is 6 in each case?
questions.solution:
Given:

The given numbers are 156, 181 and 331

After dividing by the greatest number, the remainder in each case = 6

Concept used:

The greatest number that will divide a, b, and c and leaving the same remainder in each case is given by the HCF of |a - b|, |b - c|, and |c - a|

Calculation:

Here, |156 - 181| = |- 25| = 25

|181 - 331| = |- 150| = 150

|331 - 156| = 175

Prime factors of 25 = 5 × 5

Prime factors of 150 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 5

Prime factors of 175 = 5 × 5 × 7

So, HCF of 25, 150, and 175 = 5 × 5 = 25

∴ The greatest number is 25

questions.question: A person sold an article at a loss of 18%. Had he sold it for ₹960 more, he would have gained 12%. If the article is sold for ₹3,840, then how much is the profit percentage?

questions.solution:
Let, the cost price of the article = ₹ x

⇒ (82x/100) + 960 = (112x/100) ⇒ (112x/100) - (82x/100) = 960 ⇒ (30x/100) = 960 ⇒ x = (960 × 100)/30 = 3200

The cost price of the article = ₹ 3200, Required selling price = ₹ 3840,      ⇒ Profit = 3840 - 3200 = ₹ 640

The profit percentage = (640/3200) × 100 = 20%

questions.question: In ΔACD, B and E are two points on side AC and AD respectively, such that BE is parallel to CD. CD = 9 cm, BE = 6 cm, AB = 5 cm and ED = 2 cm. What are the measures of the lengths (in cm) of AE and BC?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔACD, B and E are two points on side AC and AD respectively, such that BE is parallel to CD. CD = 9 cm, BE = 6 cm, AB = 5 cm and ED = 2 cm. What are the measures of the lengths (in cm) of AE and BC?
questions.solution:
Given:

CD = 9 cm, BE = 6 cm, AB = 5 cm and ED = 2 cm

Calculation:

Here, BE || CD

So, AB/AC = BE/CD = AE/AD

Then, AB/AC = 6/9

⇒ 5/(5 + BC) = 6/9

⇒ 6BC + 30 = 45

⇒ 6BC = 45 - 30 = 15

⇒ BC = 15/6 = 2.5 cm

Also, AE/AD = 6/9

⇒ AE/(AE + 2) = 6/9

⇒ 9AE = 6AE + 12

⇒ 9AE - 6AE = 12

⇒ 3AE = 12

⇒ AE = 12/3 = 4 cm

∴ The measures of the lengths (in cm) of AE and BC are 4 cm and 2.5 cm

questions.question: If tan 2 A + 2tanA - 63 = 0 Given that 0 < A < \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) what is the value of (2sinA + 5cosA)?
questions.questionHtml: If tan2A + 2tanA - 63 = 0 Given that 0 < A < \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) what is the value of (2sinA + 5cosA)?
questions.solution:
It is given that, tan2A + 2tanA - 63 = 0, let's assume that, tan A = x, then 

⇒ x2 + 2x - 63 = 0 ⇒ x2 + 9x - 7x - 63 = 0 ⇒ x (x + 9) - 7 (x + 9) = 0 ⇒ (x + 9) (x - 7) = 0 here, ⇒ (x - 7) = 0 ⇒ x = 7 ["-" will be neglected because 0 < A < π/2, so x ≠ -9 ] 

So, tan A = \(7\over1\) = \(p\over b\) 

Using Pythagoras Theorem, h = \(\sqrt{p^2+b^2} \) ⇒ h = \(\sqrt{7^2+1^2}\) = √50

So, 2sinA + 5cosA = [2 × \(7\over{\sqrt50}\)] + [5 × \(1\over{\sqrt50}\)] = \(14\over{\sqrt50}\) + \(5\over{\sqrt50}\) = \({14+5}\over{\sqrt50}\) = \(19\over{\sqrt50}\)

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at T. RS is a direct common tangent to the two circles touching the circles at P and Q. ∠TPQ = 42°. ∠PQT (in degrees) is:
questions.questionHtml: Two circles touch each other externally at T. RS is a direct common tangent to the two circles touching the circles at P and Q. ∠TPQ = 42°. ∠PQT (in degrees) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

∠TPQ = 42°

Concept used:

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of all angles on a straight line = 180°

Calculation:

Draw a tangent to the circles at T, intersecting QP

So, OT and OQ are two tangents to a common circle from the same external point O

Therefore, OQ = OT then ∠OQT = ∠OTQ

Also, OT and OP are two tangents to a common circle from the same external point O

Therefore, OP = OT then ∠OPT = ∠OTP

∠TPQ = 42°

Then, ∠TPQ = ∠OPT = ∠OTP = 42°

In ΔOPT, ∠OPT + ∠OTP + ∠POT = 180°

⇒ 42° + 42° + ∠POT = 180°

⇒ ∠POT = 180° - 42° - 42° = 96°

Also, ∠POT + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ 96° + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ ∠QOT = 180° - 96° = 84°

In ΔQOT, ∠OQT + ∠OTQ + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ ∠OQT + ∠OQT + 84° = 180°  [∵ ∠OQT = ∠OTQ]

⇒ 2 ∠OQT = 180° - 84°

⇒ 2 ∠PQT = 96°

⇒ ∠PQT = 96°/2 = 48°

∴ The value of ∠PQT (in degrees) is 48°

questions.question: A can finish a piece of work in 48 days and B can finish it in 60 days. They work together for 12 days and then A goes away. In how much time (in days and hours) will B finish 25% of the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a piece of work in 48 days and B can finish it in 60 days. They work together for 12 days and then A goes away. In how much time (in days and hours) will B finish 25% of the remaining work?
questions.solution:
A complete in 1 day = 1/48 work, B complete in 1 day = 1/60 work

A and B work in 1 day = (1/48) + (1/60) = 3/80 work

⇒ 12 day = (3/80) × 12 = 9/20 work,

The remaining work = 1 - (9/20) = 11/20

25% of the remaining work = (11/20) × (25/100) = 11/80 work

Time taken by B = (11/80) ÷ (1/60) = (11/80) × 60 = 33/4 days

= (33/4) × 24 hours = 198 hours = 8 days 6 hours

questions.question: A boatman can row his boat in still water at a speed of 9 km/h. He can also row 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream in 9 hours. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream?
questions.questionHtml: A boatman can row his boat in still water at a speed of 9 km/h. He can also row 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream in 9 hours. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 33 km downstream and 28 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Speed of Boat (u) = 9 km/h and Speed of Stream = v km/h.

Downstream Speed (D) = 9 + v and Upstream Speed (U) = 9 − v.

Using 44/D + 35/U = 9: By Hit and Trial, if v = 2, D = 11 and U = 7.

⇒ 44/11 + 35/7 = 4 + 5 = 9 hours (Satisfied).

New Time = 33/11 + 28/7 = 3 + 4 = 7 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.

Alternate Method

Given: Speed of boat in still water (u) = 9 km/h. Total time for 44 km downstream and 35 km upstream = 9 hours.

Formula: Time = Distance ÷ Speed; Downstream Speed (D) = u + v; Upstream Speed (U) = u − v.

⇒ 44/(9 + v) + 35/(9 − v) = 9

⇒ 44(9 − v) + 35(9 + v) = 9(81 − v2)

⇒ 396 − 44v + 315 + 35v = 729 − 9v2

⇒ 711 − 9v = 729 − 9v2

⇒ 9v2 − 9v − 18 = 0 ⇒ v2 − v − 2 = 0

⇒ (v − 2)(v + 1) = 0 ⇒ v = 2 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

⇒ Downstream Speed = 9 + 2 = 11 km/h; Upstream Speed = 9 − 2 = 7 km/h.

⇒ Required Time = 33/11 + 28/7 = 3 + 4 = 7 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.

Additional Information

Speed of Boat and Stream

Speed of boat in still water (u) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

Speed of stream (v) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed in Boats

Average speed for a round trip = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still water speed.

questions.question: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circumference of the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°. What is difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
questions.questionHtml: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circumference of the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°. What is difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
questions.solution:
∠ACB = 90° [∵ AB is diameter]

So, in ΔACB, ∠CBA = (180° - ∠ACB - ∠CAB) ⇒ ∠CBA = (180° - 90° - 42°) ⇒ ∠CBA = 48°

So, ∠CBD = (∠CBA + ∠ABD) ⇒ ∠CBD = (48° + 57°) ⇒ ∠CBD = 105°
